conventions.convention: The expectation task uses a nonempty finite law, an exactly encoded real observable in a rational interval [a,b], rational ε>0 and rational 0<δ<1. Approximate observable encoding changes the target and requires a separate error allowance.

Sample labels are distinct computational-basis vectors; each work vector has norm one, but different work vectors need not be orthogonal. Forward, inverse, controlled, value, rotation and reflection access are explicitly supplied and separately charged.
The bounded estimator returns a immediately when a=b. Otherwise 0<ε≤b−a, and it calls the unchanged QA13 median estimator with amplitude tolerance ε/(b−a).

PositiveMean uses the half-open bands [0,1), [2^(ℓ−1),2^ℓ), leaving h≥2^k in the omitted tail. Its dyadic phase size is selected by M²a²≥10^6k, and setting η_M=88/(7M) selects exactly that M through QA13.

The measured coarse value is held fixed during both conditional positive-mean calls; those calls use fresh sampler executions. Confidence schedules use certified rational upper endpoints for natural logarithms.

Prepared-copy counts exclude controlled preparation and inverse calls inside Grover rounds. Repeated controlled-Q access and supplied controlled-power access have different cost coordinates. The variance-aware accuracy guarantee assumes exact operations; approximate compilation requires a separate certified analysis.

load_bearing.statement: For an exactly encoded g:X→[a,b] and the supplied coherent sampler, a=b gives the exact answer without quantum queries. For a<b, rational 0<ε≤b−a and 0<δ<1, the estimator has additive error at most ε with probability at least 1−δ. Its median also satisfies the stated amplitude-dependent radius (b−a)(2π√(q(1−q))/M+π²/M²) with that confidence. Repeated access uses exactly r(M−1) controlled-Grover calls and O((b−a)ε⁻¹(1+ln(1/δ))) controlled-sampler/reflection queries; supplied-power access uses exactly rm separately priced power queries.

For a nonnegative finite-valued coherent-sampler output h, s=(E[h²])^(1/2), rational 0<a<1/2 and 0<ρ₁<1, PositiveMean returns u satisfying |u−E[h]|≤a(1+s)² with probability at least 1−ρ₁. With k=ceil(log₂(1/a)), it uses O(k ln(k+1)(1+ln(1/ρ₁))) prepared copies and, in repeated controlled-Q access, O(a⁻¹k^(3/2)ln(k+1)(1+ln(1/ρ₁))) state reflections. Supplied powers retain their separately declared costs.

For R≥1 independent Bernoulli variables on a finite probability space, with E[Z_i]≤p<1/2 and S their sum, Pr(S−E[S]≥t)≤exp(−2t²/R) for every t≥0. For odd R independent finite-valued estimates, each lying in an interval I with probability at least 1−p, their median lies in I except with probability at most exp(−2R(1/2−p)²).

For rational x>0, y=(x−1)/(x+1), S_N=2Σ_{j=0}^{N−1}y^(2j+1)/(2j+1), and T_N=2|y|^(2N+1)/((2N+1)(1−y²)), one has |y|<1 and |ln x−S_N|≤T_N. Increasing N from 1 until T_N≤τ terminates for every rational τ>0 and returns an enclosure of width at most 2τ.

Projective measurement of the sample register of the specified coherent sampler returns x with probability p_x; measuring the value register too returns (x,g(x)) with the same probability. Work states for different labels need not be orthogonal.

For a finite-valued coherent-sampler output v with Var(v)≤σ², known rational σ≥0, rational ε>0 and 0<ρ<1, the algorithm estimates E[v] within ε with probability at least 1−ρ. If σ=0 it returns the exact mean after one preparation. Otherwise, with L=max(2,σ/ε), its exact-access preparation count is O((1+ln(1/ρ))ln L ln ln(e^e+L)); its repeated-access state-reflection count is O((1+ln(1/ρ))L(ln L)^(3/2)ln ln(e^e+L)). Supplied-power costs and approximate compilation remain separately qualified.

seams_checked.note: Checked the counting, QFT-estimation and median interfaces against their QA29 consumers. The M≥4 restriction, exact cyclotomic outputs, rational scheduling thresholds, endpoint laws and repeated versus supplied-power costs are preserved.

Sampler registers have positive dimension and ordered computational bases. The measurement proof uses the stated tensor inner product and includes a zero-probability residual projection when sample labels do not exhaust the basis.
The unitary output is normalized, so the unit-vector projector theorem supplies the density operator used in the measurement calculation. No orthogonality of different work states is inferred.
Controlled and inverse operations remain explicit capabilities. The complete controlled Grover product retains its control phase and separately charges all factors.
The projective measurement uses mutually orthogonal projections summing to the identity, with outcome weight tr(ρP). The sampler proof derives that weight as p_x.
The rank-one and trace calculations respect the root pairing linear in its first argument and the corresponding Dirac coordinate convention.

Fresh executions and adaptive classical branch choices fit the finite query protocol. Named queries, controlled/inverse access, ordinary gates, preparation, precision and classical computation remain distinct resource coordinates.

Opened the SDP signed-sampler algorithm and matrix-expectation theorem. They supply coherent dilation and purification access, use range [−1,1] and rational sampling tolerance τ/2 with 0<τ≤2, and preserve QA29's confidence and access-mode cost qualifications.
